translations.idiomatic: V. Method for Determining Orbital Clepsydra
Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 2 chi 7 cun 1 fen 50

sentences.zh: 丈二尺二寸二分七十七

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 2 chi 2 cun 2 fen 77

sentences.zh: 丈一尺二寸一分八十二

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 1 chi 2 cun 1 fen 82

sentences.zh: 二十五刻四百七十五分
二十五刻四百七十五分
丈一尺二寸一分八十二

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 1 chi 2 cun 1 fen 82

sentences.zh: 丈二尺二寸二分七十七

translations.idiomatic: Gnomon shadow: 1 zhang 2 chi 2 cun 2 fen 77

sentences.zh: 各置其氣消息衰，依定氣所有日，每以陟降率陟減、降加其分，滿百從衰，各得每日消息定衰。

translations.literal: For each, set its qi message wane; according to the days belonging to that fixed qi, for each day apply the ascension-descent rate—subtract on ascension, add on descent—the parts; when full, carry to the wane; each obtains the daily fixed message wane.
translations.idiomatic: For each seasonal node, set its message-wane constant; for each day in that fixed qi, apply the ascension-descent rate—subtract on ascension, add on descent—to the parts; carry hundreds into the wane tally to obtain the daily fixed message wane.

sentences.zh: 其距二分前後各一氣之外，陟降不等，皆以三日為限。

translations.literal: Beyond one qi on either side of the two equinoxes, where ascension and descent are unequal, all take a three-day limit.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the single qi bracketing each equinox, where ascension and descent are unequal, a three-day band limit applies throughout.

translations.literal: On the first day of Rain Water, descent 78.
On the first day of Pure Brightness, ascension 1.
On the first day of End of Heat, descent 99.
translations.idiomatic: End of Heat, day 1: descent rate 99.

translations.literal: On the first day of Cold Dew, ascension 1.

sentences.zh: 各置初日陟降率，依限次損益之，為每日率。

translations.literal: For each, set the first day’s ascension-descent rate; according to the limit bands, increase or decrease in sequence to obtain the daily rate.
translations.idiomatic: Set each first-day ascension-descent rate; step through the limit bands by increase or decrease to obtain the daily rate.

sentences.zh: 乃遞以陟減、降加氣初消息衰，各得每日定衰。

translations.literal: Then in succession subtract ascension and add descent to the qi’s initial message wane, each obtaining the daily fixed wane.
translations.idiomatic: Then successively subtract ascension and add descent from the qi’s opening message wane to obtain the daily fixed wane.

sentences.zh: 南方戴日之下，正中無晷。

translations.literal: Beneath the sub-solar point in the south, at true center there is no gnomon shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Directly beneath the sub-solar point in the south, at true noon there is no shadow.

sentences.zh: 自戴日之北一度，乃初數千三百七十九。

translations.literal: One degree north of the sub-solar point, the initial count is 1,379.
translations.idiomatic: One degree north of the sub-solar point, the initial count is 1,379.

sentences.zh: 自此起差，每度增一，終於二十五度，計增二十六分。

translations.literal: From this the difference begins; for each degree add 1, ending at 25 degrees, totaling an increase of 26 parts.
translations.idiomatic: From here the increment begins: add 1 per degree up to 25°, for a total increase of 26 parts.

sentences.zh: 又每度增二，終於四十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 2, ending at 40 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 2 per degree up to 40°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增六，終於四十四度，增六十八。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 6, ending at 44 degrees, increase 68.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 6 per degree up to 44°, increase 68.

sentences.zh: 又每度增二，終於五十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 2, ending at 50 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 2 per degree up to 50°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增七，終於五十五度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 7, ending at 55 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 7 per degree up to 55°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增十九，終於六十度，增百六十。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 19, ending at 60 degrees, increase 160.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 19 per degree up to 60°, increase 160.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十三，終於六十五度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 33, ending at 65 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 33 per degree up to 65°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十六，終於七十度。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 36, ending at 70 degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 36 per degree up to 70°.

sentences.zh: 又每度增三十九，終於七十二度，增二百六十。

translations.literal: Again for each degree add 39, ending at 72 degrees, increase 260.
translations.idiomatic: Then add 39 per degree up to 72°, increase 260.
Each value is the per-degree difference.

sentences.zh: 因累其差，以遞加初數，滿百為分，分十為寸，各為每度晷差。

translations.literal: Accumulate the differences in succession, adding in turn to the initial count; when full, 100 become parts, and 10 parts become cun—each is the per-degree gnomon difference.
translations.idiomatic: Sum the differences cumulatively onto the initial count; carry hundreds into parts and tens of parts into cun to obtain the per-degree gnomon difference.

sentences.zh: 又累其晷差，得戴日之北每度晷數。

translations.literal: Again accumulate the gnomon differences to obtain the gnomon count for each degree north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Sum those differences again to obtain the gnomon reading for each degree north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各置其氣去極度，以極去戴日度五十六及分八十二半減之，得戴日之北度數。

translations.literal: For each, set its qi’s departure from the pole; subtract the pole’s distance from the sub-solar point, 56 degrees and 82½ parts, to obtain the degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Set the qi’s polar distance and subtract 56° 82½ parts (the pole’s offset from the sub-solar point) to obtain degrees north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各以其消息定衰所直度之晷差，滿百為分，分十為寸，得每日晷差。

translations.literal: For each, take the gnomon difference for the degree at which the fixed message wane falls; when full, 100 become parts, and 10 parts become cun, obtaining the daily gnomon difference.
translations.idiomatic: Take the per-degree gnomon difference at the degree of the fixed message wane; carry hundreds into parts and tens into cun for the daily gnomon difference.

sentences.zh: 乃遞以息減、消加其氣初晷數，得每日中晷常數。

translations.literal: Then in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial gnomon count, obtaining the daily mean noon gnomon constant.
translations.idiomatic: Then successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening gnomon count to obtain the daily mean noon gnomon constant.

sentences.zh: 以其日所在氣定小餘，爻統減之，餘為中後分。

translations.literal: Take that day’s fixed minor remainder within its qi; subtract the line divisor; the remainder is the after-noon fraction.
translations.idiomatic: Take the day’s fixed minor remainder within its qi, subtract the line divisor, and the remainder is the after-noon fraction.

sentences.zh: 不足減，反相減，為中前分。

translations.literal: If insufficient to subtract, reverse and subtract to obtain the before-noon fraction.
translations.idiomatic: If it will not subtract, reverse the subtraction to obtain the before-noon fraction.

sentences.zh: 以其晷差乘之，如通法而一，為變差。

translations.literal: Multiply by its gnomon difference; as one per universal divisor, obtaining the variation difference.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the gnomon difference, divide by the universal divisor, and obtain the variation difference.

sentences.zh: 以加減中晷常數，冬至後，中前以差減，中後以差加。

translations.literal: Add or subtract to the mean noon gnomon constant: after Winter Solstice, before noon subtract the difference, after noon add it.
translations.idiomatic: Apply it to the mean noon gnomon constant: after Winter Solstice, subtract before noon and add after noon.

sentences.zh: 夏至後，中前以差加，中後以差減。

translations.literal: After Summer Solstice, before noon add the difference, after noon subtract it.
translations.idiomatic: After Summer Solstice, add before noon and subtract after noon.

translations.literal: On Winter Solstice day, there is decrease but no increase.
translations.idiomatic: On Winter Solstice day, only decrease applies—no increase.

translations.literal: On Summer Solstice day, there is increase but no decrease.
translations.idiomatic: On Summer Solstice day, only increase applies—no decrease.

translations.literal: Obtain the daily fixed noon gnomon count.
translations.idiomatic: This yields the daily fixed noon gnomon count.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，滿象積為刻，不滿為分。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; when full of image accumulation, it becomes clepsydra marks; what does not fill becomes parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane again; carry image accumulation into clepsydra marks, leaving the remainder as parts.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息減、消加其氣初夜半漏，得每日夜半漏定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial midnight clepsydra leak, obtaining the daily fixed midnight leak count.
translations.idiomatic: Successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening midnight leak to obtain the daily fixed midnight leak.

sentences.zh: 其全刻，以九千一百二十乘之，十九乘刻分從之，如三百而一，為晨初餘數。

translations.literal: For the whole marks, multiply by 9,120; let 19 times the mark parts follow; as one per 300, obtaining the dawn-opening remainder count.
translations.idiomatic: For whole marks, multiply by 9,120, add 19 times the fractional marks, divide by 300, and obtain the dawn-opening remainder.

translations.literal: For each, double the midnight leak to obtain night marks.
translations.idiomatic: Double the midnight leak to obtain night clepsydra marks.

translations.literal: Subtract from 100 marks; the remainder is day marks.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract from 100 marks; the remainder is day marks.

sentences.zh: 減晝五刻以加夜，即晝為見刻，夜為沒刻。

translations.literal: Subtract five day marks and add to night, then day becomes appearance marks and night becomes disappearance marks.
translations.idiomatic: Move five marks from day to night: day marks become appearance marks, night marks disappearance marks.

sentences.zh: 半沒刻加半辰，起子初算外，得日出辰刻。

translations.literal: Add half the disappearance marks to half a chronogram; starting from outside the zi-opening count, obtain the sunrise chronogram mark.
translations.idiomatic: Add half disappearance marks to half a chronogram; count outward from the zi-opening tally to obtain sunrise chronogram marks.

sentences.zh: 以見刻加而命之，得日入。

translations.literal: Add appearance marks and assign it, obtaining sunset.
translations.idiomatic: Add appearance marks and assign the count to obtain sunset.

sentences.zh: 置夜刻，五而一，得每更差刻。

translations.literal: Set night marks; divide by five to obtain the per-watch difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Set night marks, divide by five, and obtain the per-watch mark difference.

translations.literal: Again divide by five to obtain the per-stave difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Divide by five again for the per-stave mark difference.

sentences.zh: 以昏刻加日入辰刻，得甲夜初刻。

translations.literal: Add dusk marks to the sunset chronogram mark, obtaining the first watch of night A.
translations.idiomatic: Add dusk marks to the sunset chronogram mark to obtain the first watch of night A.

sentences.zh: 又以更籌差加之，得五夜更籌所當辰。

translations.literal: Again add the watch-stave difference to obtain the chronogram for each watch and stave of the five night watches.
translations.idiomatic: Add the watch-stave difference repeatedly to obtain the chronogram for each watch and stave of the five night watches.

sentences.zh: 其夜半定漏，亦名晨初夜刻。

translations.literal: The fixed midnight leak is also called dawn-opening night marks.
translations.idiomatic: The fixed midnight leak is also called dawn-opening night marks.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，滿百為度，不滿為分。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; when full, 100 become degrees; what does not fill becomes parts.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane again; carry hundreds into degrees, leaving the remainder as parts.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息減、消加氣初去極度，各得每日去極定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s initial departure from the pole, each obtaining the daily fixed departure from the pole.
translations.idiomatic: Successively subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath from the qi’s opening polar distance to obtain the daily fixed polar distance.

sentences.zh: 又置消息定衰，以萬二千三百八十六乘之，如萬六千二百七十七而一，為度差。

translations.literal: Again set the fixed message wane; multiply by 12,386; as one per 16,277, obtaining the degree difference.
translations.idiomatic: Set the fixed message wane, multiply by 12,386, divide by 16,277, and obtain the degree difference.

translations.literal: When the difference fills 100, it becomes degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the difference fills 100, carry into degrees.

sentences.zh: 各遞以息加、消減其氣初距中度，得每日距中度定數。

translations.literal: For each in succession add on waning breath and subtract on growing breath from the qi’s initial distance to culminating, obtaining the daily fixed distance to culminating.
translations.idiomatic: Successively add on waning breath and subtract on growing breath from the qi’s opening distance to culmination to obtain the daily fixed culminating distance.

sentences.zh: 倍之，以減周天，為距子度。

translations.literal: Double it; subtract from the circuit of heaven to obtain the distance from zi.
translations.idiomatic: Double it, subtract from the circuit of heaven, and obtain the distance from zi.

sentences.zh: 置其日赤道日度，加距中度，得昏中星。

translations.literal: Set that day’s equatorial solar degree; add the distance to culmination to obtain the dusk culminating star.
translations.idiomatic: Take the day’s equatorial solar longitude, add culminating distance, and obtain the dusk culminating star.

sentences.zh: 倍距子度，以加昏中星，得曉中星。

translations.literal: Double the distance from zi; add to the dusk culminating star to obtain the dawn culminating star.
translations.idiomatic: Double the distance from zi, add to the dusk star, and obtain the dawn culminating star.

sentences.zh: 命昏中星為甲夜中星，加每更差度，得五夜中星。

translations.literal: Assign the dusk culminating star as the night-A culminating star; add the per-watch degree difference to obtain the culminating stars for the five night watches.
translations.idiomatic: Take the dusk culminating star as night A’s culminating star; add the per-watch degree difference for each of the five night watches.

sentences.zh: 凡九服所在，每氣初日中晷常數不齊。

translations.literal: In general, wherever the nine domains lie, the mean noon gnomon constants at each qi’s opening are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Across the nine domains, the mean noon gnomon constants at each qi’s opening are not uniform.

sentences.zh: 使每氣去極度數相減，各為其氣消息定數。

translations.literal: Have each qi’s departure-from-pole numbers subtract from one another; each difference is that qi’s fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract each qi’s polar distances pairwise; each difference is that qi’s fixed message count.

sentences.zh: 因測其地二至日晷，測一至可矣，不必兼要冬夏。

translations.literal: Then measure that place’s solstitial gnomon; measuring one solstice suffices—there is no need to require both winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Measure the locality’s solstitial gnomon; one solstice suffices—both winter and summer need not be taken.

sentences.zh: 於其戴日之北每度晷數中，較取長短同者，以為其地戴日北度數及分。

translations.literal: Among the per-degree gnomon counts north of the sub-solar point, compare and take those of equal length and shortness as that place’s degrees and parts north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Among per-degree gnomon counts north of the sub-solar point, match equal shadow lengths to fix that place’s degrees and parts north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 每氣各以消息定數加減之，因冬至後者，每氣以減。

translations.literal: For each qi, add or subtract by its fixed message count; for those after Winter Solstice, each qi subtracts.
translations.idiomatic: For each qi, apply its fixed message count; after Winter Solstice, subtract for each qi.

translations.literal: For those after Summer Solstice, each qi adds.
translations.idiomatic: After Summer Solstice, add for each qi.

translations.literal: Obtain each qi’s degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: This yields each qi’s degrees north of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 各因所直度分之晷數，為其地每定氣初日中晷常數。

translations.literal: For each, take the gnomon count for its degree and parts as that place’s fixed mean noon gnomon constant at each qi’s opening.
translations.idiomatic: Take the gnomon count at each degree and part as that locality’s fixed mean noon gnomon constant at each qi’s opening.

sentences.zh: 其測晷有在表南者，亦據其晷尺寸長短與戴日北每度晷數同者，因取其所直之度，去戴日北度數。

translations.literal: If the measured gnomon falls south of the table, likewise according to whether its gnomon’s size, length, and shortness match the per-degree counts north of the sub-solar point, thereby take the degree it corresponds to and subtract from the degrees north of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: If the measured shadow falls south of the table, match its length to the north-of-sub-solar per-degree table, take the corresponding degree, and subtract from degrees north of the sub-solar point.

translations.literal: Reverse it to obtain degrees south of the sub-solar point.
translations.idiomatic: Reverse the sign to obtain degrees south of the sub-solar point.

sentences.zh: 然後以消息定數加減之。

translations.literal: Then add or subtract by the fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Then apply the fixed message count by addition or subtraction.

sentences.zh: 二至各於其地下水漏以定當處晝夜刻數。

translations.literal: At each solstice, fix the day-and-night clepsydra marks for that place’s water clock to determine the local day and night mark count.
translations.idiomatic: At each solstice, calibrate the local water clock to fix the day-and-night clepsydra marks for that place.

translations.literal: Then subtract to obtain the solstitial difference in marks.
translations.idiomatic: Subtract the two to obtain the solstitial mark difference.

sentences.zh: 半之，以加減二至晝夜刻數，為定春秋分初日晝夜刻數。

translations.literal: Halve it; add or subtract to the solstitial day-and-night mark counts to obtain the fixed spring and autumn equinox opening day-and-night mark counts.
translations.idiomatic: Halve the difference and apply it to the solstitial day-night marks to fix the spring and autumn equinox opening day-night marks.

translations.literal: Then set each qi’s fixed message count.
translations.idiomatic: Then set each qi’s fixed message count.

sentences.zh: 以當處差刻數乘之，如二至去極差度四十七分，八十而一，所得依分前後加減初日晝夜漏刻，各得餘定氣初日晝夜漏刻。

translations.literal: Multiply by the local mark difference; as one per the solstitial departure-from-pole difference of 47 parts 80, obtaining according to parts before and after to add or subtract the opening day-and-night leak marks, each obtaining the remaining fixed qi’s opening day-and-night leak marks.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the local mark difference, divide by the solstitial polar-distance span (47 parts 80), and add or subtract the opening day-night leak marks by fractional rank to obtain each remaining fixed qi’s opening day-night leaks.

sentences.zh: 置每日消息定衰，亦以差刻乘之，差度而一，所得以息減、消加其氣初漏刻，得次日。

translations.literal: Set the daily fixed message wane; likewise multiply by the mark difference; as one per degree difference, obtaining to subtract on waning breath and add on growing breath to the qi’s opening leak marks, obtaining the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Take the daily fixed message wane, multiply by the mark difference, divide by the degree difference, and step the qi’s opening leaks by waning breath and growing breath to obtain the next day.

sentences.zh: 其求距中度及昏明中星日出入，皆依陽城法求之。

translations.literal: In seeking the distance to culmination and the dusk, dawn, and culminating stars and the sun’s entry and exit, all follow the Yangcheng method.
translations.idiomatic: Distance to culmination, dusk and dawn culminating stars, and sunrise and sunset are all found by the Yangcheng method.

sentences.zh: 仍以差刻乘之，差度而一，為今有之數。

translations.literal: Still multiply by the mark difference; as one per degree difference, this is the present-part count.
translations.idiomatic: Multiply by the mark difference and divide by the degree difference for the present-part correction.

sentences.zh: 若置其地春秋定日中晷常數與陽城每日晷數，較其同者，因其日夜半漏亦為其地定春秋分初日夜半漏。

translations.literal: If one sets that place’s fixed spring and autumn equinox mean noon gnomon constant against Yangcheng’s daily gnomon counts and compares for agreement, then according to its day the midnight leak also becomes that place’s fixed spring and autumn equinox opening midnight leak.
translations.idiomatic: Match the locality’s fixed equinox mean noon gnomon to Yangcheng’s daily table; on the matching day, its midnight leak becomes the locality’s fixed equinox opening midnight leak.

sentences.zh: 求餘定氣初日，亦以消息定數依分前後加減刻分，春分後以減，秋分後以加。

translations.literal: To seek the remaining fixed qi’s opening day, likewise use the fixed message count to add or subtract marks and parts before and after the fractional rank; after the spring equinox subtract, after the autumn equinox add.
translations.idiomatic: For each remaining fixed qi’s opening day, apply the fixed message count to marks and parts by fractional rank—subtract after spring equinox, add after autumn equinox.

translations.literal: When full of image accumulation, it becomes marks.
translations.idiomatic: Carry image accumulation into clepsydra marks.

sentences.zh: 求次日，亦以消息定衰，依陽城術求之。

translations.literal: To seek the next day, likewise use the fixed message wane and follow the Yangcheng procedure.
translations.idiomatic: For the next day, step the fixed message wane by the Yangcheng procedure.

translations.literal: This method exhausts the principle and in the main accords with thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: This method plumbs the principle and is broadly sound.

translations.literal: Yet on high mountains and level plains, viewing the sun is not equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mountain heights and level plains do not present the sun equally.

translations.literal: Compare their day gnomons; only then are length and shortness the same.
translations.idiomatic: Only when their noon shadows are compared do lengths agree.

translations.literal: Examine their water leaks; many and few differ markedly.
translations.idiomatic: Water-clock flows differ greatly in rate.

translations.literal: By this cross-check, the prior method is the sounder.
translations.idiomatic: On this comparison, the earlier method is the more reliable.
